title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Pacific Ocean Perch in the Eastern Aleutian District of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area
summary:
Federal fisheries managers have closed directed fishing for Pacific ocean perch in the Eastern Aleutians for the rest of 2025 for a group of trawl vessels. The decision was made because that group’s annual catch limit has been reached and continuing would risk going over.

This helps protect the perch population and the broader marine ecosystem by making sure the region stays within its science-based limits. It supports long-term sustainability so there are fish to catch in future seasons, which benefits fishing communities, processors, and consumers over time. It also keeps management in line with federal law and the region’s groundfish plan, avoiding the larger economic and ecological costs that can come from exceeding limits.

In the short term, the closure will be hard on trawl captains, crews, processors, and local ports that rely on directed perch trips in the Eastern Aleutians. They may face lost revenue and disrupted plans through the end of the year. While boats fishing for other species can still retain small amounts of perch within bycatch limits, targeted perch trips are off the table until January.

The National Marine Fisheries Service made the change quickly, based on new catch data available November 1, and waived the usual comment period to avoid overshooting the limit. The closure took effect at noon Alaska time on November 4 and runs through December 31. The annual allowance for this group was 551 metric tons.
